questions.question: According to the Couinaud classification of hepatic segments, which segment represents the caudate lobe?
questions.detail: Segment I is the caudate lobe, which has unique venous drainage directly into the IVC and an independent blood supply.

questions.question: Which anatomical structure separates the left hepatic lobe into medial (Segment IV) and lateral (Segments II/III) segments?
choices: C. Ligamentum teres and falciform ligament
questions.detail: The ligamentum teres and falciform ligament serve as the boundary between the medial and lateral segments of the left hepatic lobe.

questions.question: A "central scar" that shows delayed enhancement on CT or MRI is a classic feature of which benign liver lesion?
questions.detail: FNH is a hyperplastic response to a vascular malformation, and its characteristic central scar typically enhances on delayed phases.

questions.question: Which imaging feature is most specific for diagnosing a cavernous hemangioma on contrast-enhanced CT?
choices: A. Rapid uniform enhancement on arterial phase
B. Discontinuous peripheral nodular enhancement with centripetal filling
C. "Washout" on the portal venous phase
D. Persistent low attenuation on all phases
questions.detail: This centripetal "filling-in" pattern is considered pathognomonic for a simple hemangioma.

questions.question: In a patient with cirrhosis, a liver mass that demonstrates intense arterial enhancement followed by "washout" on portal venous or delayed phases is highly suggestive of:
questions.detail: Arterial hypervascularity and subsequent washout are hallmark features used in LI-RADS for the diagnosis of HCC.

questions.question: Which liver lesion is strongly associated with the use of oral contraceptives and carries a risk of life-threatening hemorrhage?
questions.detail: Hepatocellular adenomas are linked to estrogen use and have a high propensity for spontaneous rupture and bleeding.

questions.question: The "Gamna-Gandy bodies" are siderotic nodules seen in the spleen of patients with portal hypertension. On MRI, they are best visualized as:
choices: C. Signal voids (dark spots) on Gradient Echo (GRE) or SWI sequences
D. Diffuse enhancement on post-gadolinium images
E. Areas of restricted diffusion on DWI
questions.detail: Because they contain hemosiderin (iron), they cause magnetic susceptibility artifact and appear as signal voids on GRE sequences.

questions.question: The "nutmeg liver" appearance on CT represents:
choices: B. Chronic passive hepatic congestion (e.g., from right heart failure)
questions.detail: Congestion results in a mottled, reticular enhancement pattern due to dilated sinusoids and sluggish blood flow.

questions.question: Which vascular syndrome involves the thrombosis of the hepatic veins and presents with hepatomegaly, ascites, and abdominal pain?
questions.detail: Budd-Chiari syndrome is specifically defined by hepatic venous outflow obstruction.

questions.question: "Morson’s sign" or the presence of multiple peripheral hepatic calcifications in a patient from a Mediterranean or Middle Eastern region suggests:
questions.detail: Echinococcal cysts commonly present with wall calcifications or internal daughter cysts.

questions.question: Steatosis (fatty liver) is diagnosed on non-contrast CT when the liver attenuation is at least how many Hounsfield Units (HU) LESS than the spleen?
questions.detail: Diagnosis is made when the liver is <40 HU or at least 10 HU lower than the spleen attenuation.

questions.question: On MRI, "In-phase" and "Out-of-phase" T1-weighted imaging is used to identify:
questions.detail: A signal drop on out-of-phase images relative to in-phase images confirms the presence of microscopic fat.

questions.question: Which rare primary liver tumor is associated with exposure to vinyl chloride, arsenic, or Thorotrast?
questions.detail: Angiosarcoma is an aggressive liver malignancy linked to these specific environmental and industrial toxins.

questions.question: A 20-year-old patient with NO history of cirrhosis is found to have a large liver mass with a central stellate calcified scar. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.detail: Unlike FNH, the scar in fibrolamellar HCC is often calcified, does not enhance on delay, and occurs in young patients without underlying cirrhosis.

questions.question: "Von Meyenburg complexes" are multiple small, non-enhancing cystic lesions throughout the liver. These are more accurately known as:
questions.detail: These are benign ductal malformations that do not communicate with the main biliary tree.

questions.question: The normal unenhanced attenuation of the liver is 30 to 60 HU. According to the sources, what absolute attenuation value is considered "hyperattenuating"?
questions.detail: An attenuation >75 HU on non-contrast CT is hyperattenuating, most commonly caused by iron overload.

questions.question: In the context of cirrhosis, what causes the radiographic "empty gallbladder fossa sign"?
choices: A. Surgical removal of the gallbladder
B. Intrahepatic stones obstructing the cystic duct
C. Replacement of hepatic parenchyma surrounding the gallbladder with periportal fat
D. Massive enlargement of the gallbladder due to hydrops
E. Congenital absence of the gallbladder
questions.detail: Loss of liver volume in cirrhosis leads to the replacement of parenchyma with fat in the gallbladder fossa.

questions.question: According to the AAST liver injury scale, a parenchymal laceration that is 2 cm deep would be classified as which grade?
questions.detail: Grade II injuries include lacerations between 1–3 cm deep or subcapsular hematomas covering 10–50% of the surface.

questions.question: To be considered a candidate for an orthotopic liver transplant under the Milan criteria, a patient with a single HCC tumor must have a maximum tumor diameter of:
questions.detail: Milan criteria specify a single tumor <5 cm, or up to three tumors each <3 cm, without major vascular invasion.

questions.question: Which anatomical structure is responsible for separating the left hepatic lobe into medial (Segment 4) and lateral (Segments 2 and 3) segments?
choices: C. Ligamentum teres and falciform ligament
questions.detail: The ligamentum teres and falciform ligament define the boundary between the medial and lateral left lobe segments.

questions.question: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD) is a type of lymphoma that can arise after solid organ transplants. It is primarily caused by which virus?
questions.detail: PTLD is caused by EBV and is managed by modifying immunosuppression levels.

questions.question: Which specific measurement ratio is highly suggestive of cirrhosis when evaluating the morphology of the liver?
choices: A. Left lobe to right lobe ratio > 0.5
B. Caudate to right lobe size ratio > 0.65
D. Portal vein to hepatic artery ratio > 2.0
questions.detail: The caudate lobe often hyper-trophies in early cirrhosis because it has independent drainage into the IVC, resulting in a ratio >0.65.

questions.question: A liver injury that involves a laceration or destruction of more than 75% of one hepatic lobe is classified by the AAST as:
questions.detail: Grade V is a severe parenchymal injury involving >75% of a lobe or injury to central hepatic veins.

questions.question: Focal Nodular Hyperplasia (FNH) is often referred to as a "stealth lesion" because:
choices: A. It is only visible on nuclear medicine scans
B. It lacks a blood supply
C. It resembles background liver parenchyma on almost all imaging modalities
D. It disappears after contrast administration
E. It is too small to be seen on CT
questions.detail: FNH consists of near-normal but disorganized liver tissue, making it difficult to differentiate from background parenchyma without specialized contrast.

questions.question: On MRI, how does a liver with significant iron overload typically appear across all sequences?
choices: A. Hyperintense relative to the spleen
B. Hypointense relative to the paraspinal muscles
C. Bright on T1 and dark on T2
E. Unchanged from a normal liver
questions.detail: An iron-overloaded liver is hypointense (dark) on all sequences compared to the paraspinal muscles.
